Συναυλία

«Τρισεύγενη»

Παρασκευή 4 Δεκεμβρίου στις 20:30 · Μέγαρο Μουσικής Αθηνών · €25
Αγοράστε εισιτήρια →

The Megaron's main stage holds a cello, a piano, and a screen. The light changes. You hear the opening phrase—something classical dissolves into something else. The images come in, and they're not supplementing the music. They're disagreeing with it. Complicating it. Asking it questions.

"Τρισεύγενη" (Thrice-Begotten, or Threefold-Born) is a collaboration between composer Thodoris Athanasiou and filmmaker Sofia Exarchou. It sits in the gap between concert and visual art, letting each discipline speak its own language while the audience navigates the contradiction. The cello carries the weight. The piano traces implications. The film suggests what neither sound nor silence can quite articulate.

This is post-concert music—classical training deployed for contemporary purposes. The Megaron's acoustics mean every gesture in the cello bow creates a physical event. Every sustain becomes a room-filling meditation.

The audience is split: serious classical attendees who trust the Megaron's programming, contemporary art followers who respect Exarchou's work, and people who saw the title and intuited something interesting. All of them come prepared to be thoughtful. This isn't crowd energy; it's collective attention. The room respects silence between phrases.

The piece unfolds in movements, but not in the classical sense. First section establishes the three-part structure (music, image, the space between them). Middle section deepens each element separately—cello goes one direction, film goes another. Final movement brings them back into conversation, but transformed. By the end, you're not sure whether the film was always there or whether the music created it.

| Aspect | Details | |--------|---------| | **Setting** | Megaron main hall, 1,960-seat concert venue, professional staging | | **Vibe** | Sophisticated, contemplative, intellectually demanding, visually engaged | | **Format** | Contemporary classical + film projection, ~60 minutes | | **Doors** | Standard seating, no restricted views |

If you need a clear emotional arc or resolution, this will feel unfinished. The point is the unfinished-ness. But if you want to sit in a major cultural institution while something legitimately new is being attempted—if you trust your own ability to make meaning from the gap between disciplines—the Megaron's resources are behind this experiment.
